value.anchor: GC-04 PDF pp6-7 Fig10: measured 180 ns whole compute includes precharge, DTC/MAC and 5b SAR. This anchors only the overall scale; it does not identify individual stages in the adapted frontend.
value.conditions: Retain native 64-cell bitline load, 700 nA endpoint, 200 fF effective integration capacitance per branch and +/-224 mV differential range. Main early_release uses 1 ns MAC and 64 ns single-pair refresh integration. Existing CCTRL/PRE/SAMP and tunable RWL separate precharge, integration and sampled SAR; binary-input rounds have no outstanding longer RWL pulse. The entire 36/86/136 ns common precharge/select/reconnect-settle/isolate-sample/recovery allowance remains, with shared TI/TA/TD separately charged. No additional ADC, hold bank, driver or shadow is needed to advance the existing sampling boundary; no 63 ns mandatory device settling was identified. Phase allowances are engineering references, not measured stage times. Writing isolates added integration/SAR capacitance and retains approximately original 50 fF program load.

phase_evidence.confirmed: Distinct precharge, variable-RWL MAC and sampled SAR phases; single-row retention reads tune RWL pulse to ADC range. The source reports no separated adapted 1/64 ns phase budget.
phase_evidence.common_physical_conditions: Same selected 64-cell local bitline, effective integration load, endpoint current, full-scale range and ADC; different number of active rows and RWL width. Equal worst-case integrated charge does not prove equal settling/noise.
phase_evidence.assumed_common_stages: Aggregate precharge, selection, load reconnect/settle, sample and recovery; no unsupported numerical subdivision of the 36/86/136 ns allowance.
phase_evidence.qualification: Mode-specific scheduling uses existing CCTRL, PRE/SAMP switching, tunable pulse generation and independent SAR start. The 1 ns pulse is followed by all allocated settling/isolation/sample operations; early release does not mean zero post-pulse settling. Fixed 64 ns control reservation is a conservative comparison. The 180 ns source full cycle is only a scale anchor, not a measured decomposition or measured speedup.
phase_evidence.control_dependency: GC-04 PDF p.6 III.B and p.7 Fig.10 expose independent PRE/SAMP and variable RWL control. p.10 retention read tunes RWL for a single active row. With one-bit inputs all active RWLs finish at 1 ns in the reference MAC, so no 64 ns refresh pulse or unfinished input phase shares that evaluation. Common residual, TI, TA and two digital reconstruction ticks remain mandatory.
phase_evidence.clock_qualification: TD budgets digital reconstruction/control; analog pulse and phase edges use the already tunable delay/phase control. No evidence requires every analog phase to occupy an integer TD count. Short/reference/long retain full 36/86/136 ns common overhead with no fabricated internal ns split; timing closure remains a reference-design condition.

source_excerpts.value: Disconnect added integration/SAR sampling capacitance during programming using local switches; source 65 ns write anchor assumes approximately original 50 fF BL load including switch parasitics. Reconnect/settle is included in dedicated read slot; if write load increases, 65 ns must be revalidated/rebudgeted.
